c74object.name: evi.freqshift.weaver~
c74object.digest: Time domain frequency shifter after D. K. Weaver's 'third method'
c74object.description:
evi.freqshift.weaver~ is a 'max define' for the evi_freqshift_weaver.gendsp gen~ abstraction. Because evi.freqshift.weaver~ is a 'max define' it also accepts all messages and attributes that a gen~ object does.
Time domain frequency shifter. Not like MSP freqshift~. An implementation of D. K. Weaver's famous 'third method' (unlike freqshift~, fbinshift~ and evi.freqshift.hilbert~ which implement the more usual hilbert filtering 'second method'). N.B. no filtering shift here, all done with quadrature oscillators and lowpass filters.

inlet.digest: Inlet #2: (use freqsmooth attr) Frequency Shift in ± Hz
inlet.description: The main control, frequency shift in Hz +/- 0. Can be optionally smoothed with the @freqsmooth attribute.

inlet.digest: Inlet #3: Frequency Shift FM in ± Hz
inlet.description: Audio rate FM of frequency shift (from inlet 2).

Naive reset of quadrature oscillator phases. Note that in 'evi.freqshift.weaver~' this reset need not be used, as a major feature of the internal gen~ code is that it does automatic and clickless resetting of phase itself (depending on the 'resetauto' attribute, which is on by default).

outlet.description: The audio output of the frequency shifter.

outlet.digest: Outlet #2: fake quadOsc Cos (if oscout attr)
outlet.description: If @oscout attribute is active, this provides the Cosine Quad Oscillator output. If @oscout is off, nothing comes out of this outlet. Note that this signal is not the real Quad Oscillator output as the real oscillator is in a very high range in Weaver's method. Instead this is a multiplied down osciallator which might be useful for downstream processing.

outlet.digest: Outlet #3: fake quadOsc Sin (if oscout attr)
outlet.description: If @oscout attribute is active, this provides the Sine Quad Oscillator output. If @oscout is off, nothing comes out of this outlet. Note that this signal is not the real Quad Oscillator output as the real oscillator is in a very high range in Weaver's method. Instead this is a multiplied down osciallator which might be useful for downstream processing.

attribute.name: detune
attribute.description: Detune is in cents, applied ± 1 semitone. This detunes the main quadrature oscillators and the fixed frequency crossover filters, giving a strange and unsubtle effect.

attribute.name: drive
attribute.description: Internally the object uses an instance of 'evi.sinfold~' to waveshape the upper and lower sidebands depending on the @saturation attribute state. Increasing the drive will saturate the sidebands harder. By default @saturation is off.

attribute.name: freqsmooth
attribute.description: Optionally smooth the frequency shifting control (input 2). This can safely be used even if using the audio FM (inlet 3) as it is not applied to the FM signal.

attribute.name: highpass
attribute.description: This applies highpasses to the sidebands for taming bass response. It is not smoothed and thus probably best used as a static tool only.

attribute.name: oscout
attribute.description: If active, the object will instantiate an additional quad oscillator at the given frequency shift in order to use for downstream processing. This is available at outlets 2 and 3. This is not the actual internal quad oscillator as that is not at a useful frequency in Weaver's method. If off (the default), nothing is computed or output from outlets 2 and 3.

attribute.name: resetauto
attribute.description: If active (the default), the object automatically and sample accurately cleanly and clicklessly resets the phase of the internal quad oscillator when required. If off, this may cause dc or click when resetting manually (inlet 4).

attribute.name: saturation
attribute.description: If active, a waveshaping distortion algorithm is applied to the sidebands in different ways depending on @select. If off (the default) the output is clean digital frequency shifting, if on the output is saturated and can be driven via the @drive attribute. Using saturation increases CPU usage.

attribute.name: select
attribute.description: Select the audio algorithm available at the main audio output (outlet 1). 0=Upper and Lower Sidebands mixed, 1=Lower Sideband (default), 2=strange but cool effect with Upper and Lower Sidebands in an AM (amplitude modulation) configuration. Note, for modes 0 and 1, if @shiftmode == 0.5 the frequency shifting effect is cancelled out!

attribute.name: shiftmode
attribute.description: A very strange attribute. At '0' the object abides by the D. K. Weaver lowpass filtering algorithm and oscillators are post filter. At '1' the object reverses this algorithm and oscillators are pre filter. Interpolating between the two can give very interesting results. Note, if @select is set to 0 or 1, and @shiftmode == 0.5, the frequency shifting effect is cancelled out! The object is happy smoothly interpolating through this state.

attribute.name: smooth
attribute.description: Smooth all internal parameters (apart from the frequency shift inlet 2, which has it's own smoothing amount via @freqsmooth) by this amount of time in ms.
